analysis.title: A Lot of Doughnuts
key_insights: US long/short net leverage fell to 43.4%, the 0th percentile over the past five years (GS Prime).
The US fundamental long/short ratio (market value) also fell to the 0th percentile on a five-year view (GS Prime).
Global equity long/short net leverage is around the 2nd-3rd percentile (JPM PI).
Despite the de-risking, global hedge funds were down 3.3% month to date after Thursday's selloff, versus a 0.2% gain for the S&P 500 (JPM PI). Hedge fund alpha has suffered.
AI has zero outperformance versus the overall market: the S&P 500 ex AI has overtaken the S&P 500 on YTD returns (GS trading desk).
Jefferies' trading desk was net for sale in Tech by more than $1B on 7 of the last 10 days, and described the 20-day net selling as one of the more dramatic Tech selling periods in recent years.
Hedge fund Magnificent Seven exposure is not washed out: net Mag 7 exposure is at the 81st percentile since 2020 and the 77th percentile over the past year (MS PB).
The author notes the contrarian read is that positioning this low should be bullish, but says it does not feel right this time.

sector_views.rationale: Jefferies' desk was net for sale in Tech by more than $1B on 7 of the last 10 days, and AI-related stocks no longer outperform the S&P 500.

risk_factors: Hedge funds have cut exposure without protecting returns, so de-risking has not delivered hedging benefits.
Mag 7 exposure remains elevated relative to the rest of the book, which leaves room for further selling.
Continued heavy net selling in Tech by institutional desks.
